answer: An agent market assigns voting power in proportion to tokens locked for 90 days, rather than the number of registered identities. Whether an agent trades basalt, maps a glacier, or tracks the sun’s zenith, the same rule applies: splitting 100 tokens among a thousand accounts still buys only 100 tokens’ worth of influence. To gain more power, an attacker must acquire and immobilize more tokens, paying acquisition costs and forgoing other uses of that capital.
